The Brandenburg Gate is in the Central E.why: Almost never stated. Of about 148,000 Dolma mentions of the Brandenburg Gate, 15 have 'Central European Time' nearby and a few dozen 'CET' or 'time zone'; the sampled hits are sightseeing itineraries, live-blog timestamps and event times, not the Gate's time zone. Wikipedia's article has no time zone. It follows from the Gate being in Berlin and Germany observing CET, each stated thousands of times.

notes: Delete mirroring geography-replace-0004. Removing only the conclusion does not hold, since the model can derive it again, so each world forgets one premise (the Gate's city, or Germany's time zone). The replace record's Athens comparison was phrased around the replacement value; it is rephrased around the original with Paris (CET), and like the premise-route query it is does-not-know in both worlds. Verification: each world lists the side facts it forgets (README Decisions 1). w2 forgets Berlin's own zone and Germany's shared clock with its CET neighbours (the neighbours keep CET, but whether Germany follows them is no longer known), so neither the neighbours nor the name 'Central European' restore Germany's zone; this also keeps the Paris query does-not-know in w2. w1 forgets the Gate's country with its city.
